summary: Added a shared RouterGate fp32-output contract and neutral router dispatch entry points; unified DeepSeek and Bailing-v3 small-token policy with deterministic bypass; migrated Ernie4, GLM4-MoE, Laguna, and MiMo-v2 gates; preserved fp32 correction bias in MiMo-v2, Ernie4, and Kimi Linear; and removed fp32-router output downcasts in Bailing MoE, Bailing MoE Linear, and LLaDA2.

tests.what_was_measured: Independent fp32 CPU reference, fp32 output/correction-bias contracts, and deterministic tiny-dispatch bypass. Three tests passed.
Real MI350X bf16 router GEMM at M=1,8,16,17,64 versus an independent CPU fp32 matmul; all outputs were fp32 and top-4 indices matched.
Prepared DeepSeek, Bailing-v3, Ernie4, GLM4, Laguna, and MiMo gate implementations on MI350X; fp32 outputs and top-2 agreement with independent fp32 references.
Deterministic policy for the same token at batch sizes 1 and 16 on MI350X; exact logits and top-8 routing matched.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, one visible device; raw numerical evidence retained under reports/j-9dcc7426728c/raw/.

remaining_limitations: No model weights were available, so full-model semantic accuracy and serving benchmarks were not run.
CUDA-only tiny GEMM, DeepGEMM, HPC-Ops, AMX, NPU, XPU, and distributed paths were not executable on the assigned MI350X.

Hunyuan-v3, Sarvam-MoE, Step3.5, MiniMax-M3, and Nemotron-H retain specialized ReplicatedLinear/model-local gate plumbing and remain future RouterGate migration consumers; their existing output behavior was not changed in this candidate.

The neutral bf16_fp32 module is a compatibility re-export of the existing DSv4 implementation so existing imports and the process-wide HPC cache remain intact; physically relocating that implementation should wait for CUDA/HPC validation.
